overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what has been added around the basic language model. You'll be asked about step-by-step reasoning and reasoning models, retrieval, tool use, and agents and memory, including what each fixes and how each can fail.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why does having a model write out intermediate steps improve its accuracy on multi-step problems?

options.html: Writing steps retrains the model's parameters as it goes along
options.text: Writing steps retrains the model's parameters as it goes along
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Parameters don't change while a model writes. Each written step becomes part of the text the next token is predicted from, so one hard prediction is replaced by several easier ones.

options.html: Writing steps lets the model look up the answer in its training text
options.text: Writing steps lets the model look up the answer in its training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A model doesn't consult its training text. Each written step becomes part of the text the next token is predicted from, so one hard prediction is replaced by several easier ones.

options.html: Each written step becomes context for the next prediction
options.text: Each written step becomes context for the next prediction
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model predicts each token from all the text so far, including what it has just written. With partial results on the page, each next step is an easier prediction.

options.html: Each written step is checked by a separate calculator program
options.text: Each written step is checked by a separate calculator program
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That would be tool use, which is a different addition. Each written step becomes part of the text the next token is predicted from, so one hard prediction is replaced by several easier ones.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant with web search gives an answer with a link beside one sentence. What does the link show?

options.html: That the sentence was copied word for word from the linked page
options.text: That the sentence was copied word for word from the linked page
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A model can misquote or misread a page it retrieved. The link shows which page was retrieved, and you have to open it to see whether the sentence matches.

options.html: That the linked page has been checked and found to be reliable
options.text: That the linked page has been checked and found to be reliable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing in retrieval checks a page's reliability. The link shows which page was retrieved, and you have to open it to see whether the sentence matches.

options.html: That the model's parameters now include the linked page's content
options.text: That the model's parameters now include the linked page's content
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Retrieval places text in the context window and leaves the parameters unchanged. The link shows which page was retrieved, and you have to open it to see whether the sentence matches.

options.html: That the linked page was retrieved for the model to work from
options.text: That the linked page was retrieved for the model to work from
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A citation shows what was retrieved. It doesn't show that the model read the page correctly, so the claim still needs to be compared with the source.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant returns an exact total for a column of figures, and the total is wrong. The calculator tool worked properly. What most likely happened?

options.html: The model gave the calculator the wrong numbers
options.text: The model gave the calculator the wrong numbers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The tool is dependable, and the model's choice of input is a prediction. A calculator gives an exact answer to whatever it's handed.

options.html: The calculator rounded the figures to save computing time
options.text: The calculator rounded the figures to save computing time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The scenario says the tool worked properly. The likeliest cause is that the model passed it the wrong numbers, since choosing the input is a prediction by the model.

options.html: The model's parameters were changed by the calculation
options.text: The model's parameters were changed by the calculation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Using a tool doesn't change a model's parameters. The likeliest cause is that the model passed the tool the wrong numbers, since choosing the input is a prediction by the model.

options.html: The calculator's result was too long for the context window
options.text: The calculator's result was too long for the context window
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A single total is a few tokens. The likeliest cause is that the model passed the tool the wrong numbers, since choosing the input is a prediction by the model.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these limits of a language model working alone can retrieval address? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It holds nothing from after its training text ends
options.text: It holds nothing from after its training text ends
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Current pages can be fetched and placed in the context window when you ask.

options.html: It has never seen your organization's private documents
options.text: It has never seen your organization's private documents
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Documents can be supplied for the conversation, and the model can answer from them.

options.html: It can misread a passage that is in front of it
options.text: It can misread a passage that is in front of it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Retrieval supplies the passage, and the model can still misread, misquote, or ignore it.

options.html: It can't show where an answer came from
options.text: It can't show where an answer came from
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An answer built on supplied text can point to that text, which makes it possible to check.

forms.stemHtml: An agent misreads a figure early in a long task, saves it in a note, and bases its later comparisons on the note. What is this an example of?

options.html: Prompt sensitivity, because the wording of the task changed
options.text: Prompt sensitivity, because the wording of the task changed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing in the scenario involves rewording. An early mistake that later steps build on is a compounding error.

options.html: A compounding error, because later steps build on it
options.text: A compounding error, because later steps build on it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In a loop, each step takes earlier steps as given, so an early mistake carries forward into everything built on it.

options.html: A knowledge cutoff, because the figure was too recent to know
options.text: A knowledge cutoff, because the figure was too recent to know
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The agent had the source in front of it and misread it. An early mistake that later steps build on is a compounding error.

options.html: Code execution, because the agent ran a program it had written
options.text: Code execution, because the agent ran a program it had written
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No program is involved in the scenario. An early mistake that later steps build on is a compounding error.

title: Reasoning, tools, and agents
